output:
## Overview

Your chart is built around the Life Palace in Xu 戌, which holds Ju Men (the eloquent talker and debater, sharp with words and ideas) in its fallen brightness. The Body Palace — the secondary marker that shows where your energy settles in adult life, while the Life Palace shows the core self — sits in Chen 辰 in the Travel Palace, and carries Tian Tong (the easygoing comfort-lover, fond of harmony and good living) with Hua Lu (prosperity). Your Five Element Bureau is Wood 3, a fairly light and flexible number that tends to suit a life of movement, learning and adaptation rather than heavy, fixed structures.

Two features stand out. First, the tension between the inward, verbal Life Palace and the outgoing, comfort-seeking Body Palace: much of your life story involves moving between thinking and talking about things, and actually going out into the world to enjoy them. Second, the wealth axis: Tai Yang (the sun, public spirit, visibility and generosity) sits bright in the Wealth Palace, while the Property Palace across from it holds Lian Zhen (the principled but complicated charmer) with Hua Ji (obstacle, where extra care is needed) alongside Qi Sha (the disciplined fighter). Money flows well through visible, generous effort, but property and fixed assets ask for patience.

## Life Palace and Personality

Ju Men in the Life Palace is the star of speech, argument, analysis and persuasion. In fallen brightness, its gifts come with a twist: you may be quick to spot the flaw in an argument, quick to voice a correction, and sometimes quicker to debate than to listen. This is not a flaw so much as a dial that needs setting. People with this placement often do well in roles where critical thinking is valued — editing, law-like reasoning, teaching, writing, consulting, troubleshooting — because the mind is genuinely sharp. The work is to choose when to speak and when to let a point go.

The Life Palace has no supporting stars of its own from the six auspicious or six challenging stars, which keeps the core personality relatively uncluttered: what you see is mostly Ju Men, direct and verbal. Across from it, in the Travel Palace, Tian Tong with Hua Lu softens the picture considerably. Tian Tong brings a liking for ease, food, company and comfort, and Hua Lu adds a steady supply of small pleasures and helpful openings when you are out in the world — travelling, meeting people, changing scenery. The Body Palace sitting here suggests that your best self often emerges away from home and routine, and that good things tend to arrive through movement rather than staying put.

Because the Body Palace is also where Tuo Luo (delay and drag), Huo Xing (sudden flare and impatience) and Ling Xing (sharp nervous energy) all sit, out-in-the-world energy can sometimes run hot and then stall. The practical translation: you tend to do well when you travel or socialise with a loose plan, and less well when you push hard for immediate results. Give journeys, moves and new ventures a little slack in the schedule.

## Career

The Career Palace in Yin 寅 is empty, so it works through borrowed stars from the Spouse Palace: Tian Ji (the strategist and problem-solver, always thinking a move ahead) in steady brightness and Tai Yin (the gentle, reflective Moon, skilled with detail and atmosphere) in fair brightness. An empty Career Palace with strong borrowed stars often means the career identity is flexible — you may wear several hats, change direction more than once, or find that your work is shaped by a partner or by collaboration. Tian Ji favours planning, systems, analysis and advisory work; Tai Yin favours quiet craftsmanship, research, writing, care work and anything that rewards sensitivity to mood and detail.

Dikong (the void star, which can hollow out effort if it is scattered) also sits in the Career Palace. This is best read as a call for focus: spreading effort across too many projects tends to leave less behind than concentrating on one or two. The presence of Dikong with borrowed Tian Ji actually suits work that is conceptual or idea-led — strategy, design, teaching, content — where the "product" is thought rather than inventory.

The direction of travel is reinforced by the next Major Period, which falls in this Career Palace from the age of 43. Career questions tend to become central in the coming decade, and the planning instincts of Tian Ji are a good thing to develop now: keep a written plan, review it seasonally, and build one clear specialism rather than many shallow ones.

## Wealth

The Wealth Palace holds Tai Yang in bright brightness — the sun at its strong phase, associated with generosity, visibility, reputation and public-facing work. This is one of the more fortunate money signatures: income tends to come through being seen, being useful to a wide circle, and doing work that has a public or communicative dimension. It is not a hoarding star; Tai Yang gives and receives in roughly equal measure, which generally rewards fair dealing and open-handedness but can leak money through generosity if it goes unmanaged.

Two challenging stars sit here too: Qing Yang (the blunt blade, direct and sometimes abrasive) and Ling Xing (the sharp spark, restless and quick to react). Together they suggest money decisions made in a hurry or out of irritation tend to be the ones you regret. A simple rule helps: any financial decision worth making is worth sleeping on for a few nights. The Property Palace — the palace of fixed assets and long-term holdings — carries Lian Zhen with Hua Ji, which is a clear signal to be careful and slow with property matters, contracts and large commitments. Read the fine print, ask questions, and avoid rushing into anything that cannot be undone.

The Property Palace also holds Qi Sha in brilliant brightness, the disciplined fighter star. Handled well, this is the energy that builds something durable through persistence and structure. The tension between Qi Sha's drive and Lian Zhen's Hua Ji is the crux: steady, methodical accumulation suits you far better than bold moves or quick turnover.

## Love and Partnership

The Spouse Palace in Shen 申 is one of the strongest in the chart. Tian Ji sits here in steady brightness with Hua Quan (power), and Tai Yin in fair brightness. Tian Ji in the Spouse Palace often points to a partner who is intelligent, adaptable and mentally quick — someone who plans, problem-solves and likes to talk things through. Hua Quan adds a decisive, capable quality: your partner is likely to have a mind of their own and a desire to lead in domestic decisions. That is generally a strength, as long as the two of you agree who leads on what.

Tai Yin in the Spouse Palace softens the picture, suggesting emotional sensitivity and a reflective side in the relationship or in the kind of person you are drawn to. Dikong also sits in the Spouse Palace, which is worth watching rather than fearing: it can show up as a feeling of distance at times, or as periods where one of you is preoccupied. Naming that openly tends to dissolve it faster than trying to fix it silently.

The empty Career Palace borrows exactly these two stars, which links work and partnership closely. A partner may be a collaborator, or your relationship may grow through shared professional or intellectual ground. In 2027 and 2028, Tai Yin and Tian Ji pick up further transformations in this palace, which makes partnership themes more prominent; these are good years to invest care in communication and shared plans. "Invest" here means time and attention, not money.

## Wellbeing Habits

The Health Palace in Si 巳 holds Wu Qu (the steady, disciplined worker, associated with structure and endurance) and Po Jun (the pioneer who clears the old to build the new), both in neutral brightness. This combination tends to favour routine over improvisation: your body generally responds well to a regular rhythm of sleep, meals and movement, and less well to erratic schedules and sudden bursts of overexertion followed by collapse. Po Jun in particular suggests you benefit from variety within a structure — the same walk every day may bore you, but a rotating mix of movement keeps the energy moving.

The Life Palace's Ju Men is a verbal, mental star, so your mind can run hot. Sleep is the first place this shows: a wind-down ritual that gets you off screens and out of debate mode before bed tends to help more than it would for most people. Food-wise, the Body Palace's Tian Tong with Hua Lu enjoys rich, social eating, which is lovely in moderation; keeping meals roughly regular and not skipping them in busy stretches supports the Wu Qu need for consistency.

For emotional balance, the Ju Men tendency to argue a point to its end, combined with the Travel Palace's Huo Xing impatience and Ling Xing sharpness, suggests building in a pause before reacting — even a short walk or a few slow breaths. Movement that involves the outdoors suits the Body Palace in the Travel Palace: walking, cycling, being outside. If you feel unwell, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.

## Family and Social Circle

The Friends Palace in Mao 卯 is empty and borrows Zi Wei (the emperor, dignified and authoritative) in bright brightness and Tan Lang (the charmer, sociable and pleasure-seeking) in fair brightness from the Siblings Palace. This is a sociable signature: your wider circle is likely to include capable, impressive people with strong personalities, and your standing among them can be good. Zuo Fu, the helpful deputy star, sits in the Friends Palace, which points to genuine support from friends when you ask for it — the key word being "ask".

The Parents Palace in Hai 亥 holds Tian Xiang (the loyal minister, dignified and dutiful) in steady brightness, with You Bi and Tian Kui, two of the six auspicious stars. This is a warm and supportive combination for the relationship with parents and elders, and for mentors or authority figures generally: people in senior positions tend to be helpful to you, and structured, respectful relationships with them pay off.

The Siblings Palace in You 酉 carries Zi Wei and Tan Lang (borrowed by the Friends Palace), plus Tian Yue, the auspicious star of helpful people. Siblings or close peers may be strong-willed and prominent, and they can be useful allies. The Children Palace in Wei 未 has Tian Fu (the treasurer, steady and reliable) in brilliant brightness, with Wen Chang (learning and refinement) and Wen Qu (expression and academic polish) both transformed by Hua Ke (recognition). If you have or work with children, they are likely to be steady and bright, and educational or creative recognition is a recurring theme. The Property Palace's Lian Zhen with Hua Ji is the one place in the family picture that asks for patience: keep family dealings over property and money clear and written down.

## Major Period and Year by Year

Your current Major Period runs from age 33 to 42 and falls in the Property Palace in Chou 丑, which holds Lian Zhen in fair brightness with Hua Ji, and Qi Sha in brilliant brightness. Ten years focused on home, property and foundations, then, with a mixture of drive and friction. Qi Sha gives the period its pace — determined, disciplined, capable of long effort — while Lian Zhen's Hua Ji marks the area that asks for care: contracts, family finances, and anything involving shared assets or the home. The productive way through this decade is methodical: one project at a time, paperwork in order, and patience when things move slower than you would like.

The next Major Period, ages 43 to 52, falls in the Career Palace in Yin 寅, an empty palace borrowing Tian Ji and Tai Yin from the Spouse Palace. The spotlight shifts from the home base to work, strategy and collaboration; the pace becomes more thoughtful and planning-led, and partnership or teamwork tends to shape career moves. Annual pillars follow the Chinese lunar year and roughly match the calendar year.

### 2026 丙午 · Bing Wu

The Wealth Palace becomes the annual Life Palace, bringing Tai Yang in bright brightness to the foreground, with Qing Yang and Ling Xing alongside. This is a year for visible effort and reputation-building, with money themes prominent. Tian Tong takes Hua Lu in the Travel Palace, so travel, new surroundings and social ease bring openings; Tian Ji takes Hua Quan in the Spouse Palace, giving a partner or close collaborator a stronger voice in decisions; Wen Chang takes Hua Ke in the Children Palace, favouring study, creative work and recognition for younger people or projects. Lian Zhen takes Hua Ji in the Property Palace, the same palace as your Major Period: property and family financial matters deserve extra care and a slower pace, especially early in the year. Lean into visible work and travel; hold back from rushing property decisions.

### 2027 丁未 · Ding Wei

The Children Palace becomes the annual Life Palace, with Tian Fu in brilliant brightness, Wen Chang and Wen Qu. This is a year oriented toward creativity, learning and the next generation in a broad sense — projects you nurture. Tai Yin takes Hua Lu in the Spouse Palace and Tian Ji takes Hua Ke there too, making this a warm and communicative year for partnership; Tian Tong takes Hua Quan in the Travel Palace, so journeys and outside opportunities carry authority. Ju Men takes Hua Ji in the Life Palace itself, which suggests words carry extra weight this year: keep an eye on sharp remarks, especially with people closest to you. In the first half, put energy into partnership conversations; in the second half, creative and family projects tend to flow.

### 2028 戊申 · Wu Shen

The Spouse Palace becomes the annual Life Palace, with Tian Ji and Tai Yin, so partnership is the year's central theme. Tan Lang takes Hua Lu in the Friends Palace, bringing sociable and enjoyable energy through your wider circle; Tai Yin takes Hua Quan in the Spouse Palace, giving the relationship more decisiveness; You Bi takes Hua Ke in the Parents Palace, so elders and mentors offer recognition and help. Tian Ji takes Hua Ji in the Spouse Palace, meaning the same palace where partnership is highlighted also asks for care — a sign to make space for listening, and to avoid letting planning turn into overthinking. Your Major Period shifts into the Career Palace this year, so work matters gain new weight. Autumn is a good time to set work goals for the new decade.

### 2029 己酉 · Ji You

The Siblings Palace becomes the annual Life Palace, with Zi Wei and Tan Lang, and Tian Yue, the helpful-people star. Peers, siblings and close collaborators take centre stage, and support from them is worth asking for. Wu Qu takes Hua Lu in the Health Palace, a good year to build physical routine; Tan Lang takes Hua Quan in the Siblings Palace, giving peers initiative and drive; Tian Liang takes Hua Ke in the Wellbeing Palace, so reflective or spiritual pursuits bring recognition and peace. Wen Qu takes Hua Ji in the Children Palace, so creative or educational matters involving younger people or expressive projects need patience — check details before committing. Spring and summer are good for collaboration; keep the slower pace for creative follow-through.

### 2030 庚戌 · Geng Xu

The Life Palace itself becomes the annual Life Palace, with Ju Men in fallen brightness. This is a year of self-definition — of speaking about who you are and what you stand for. Tai Yang takes Hua Lu in the Wealth Palace, which is favourable for income and reputation; Wu Qu takes Hua Quan in the Health Palace, so physical discipline and routine carry weight; Tai Yin takes Hua Ke in the Spouse Palace, supporting harmony in partnership; Tian Tong takes Hua Ji in the Travel Palace, so travel and outside commitments ask for care — build in margin, and don't over-pack the schedule. Toward the end of the year, this is a good time to review how you speak about yourself and your work, and to refine the message for the decade ahead.

## Guidance

- Put one written rule around property and family finances, since Lian Zhen with Hua Ji sits in your Property Palace: no large commitment without a second reading and a few days' pause.
- Build one clear specialism in your work, given the empty Career Palace borrowing Tian Ji and Tai Yin plus the presence of Dikong: focus tends to outperform breadth for you.
- Start a wind-down ritual before bed and keep meal times roughly regular, supporting Ju Men in the Life Palace and Wu Qu in the Health Palace.
- Ask friends for help explicitly — Zuo Fu in the Friends Palace means support tends to be available when requested, and less so when assumed.
- Set a personal rule of sleeping on financial decisions, since Qing Yang and Ling Xing in the Wealth Palace make quick reactions the ones most likely to misfire.
